Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AeroGreen Energy Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. At that time, instructions will be given on how to ask questions using your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss AeroGreen Energy Corp.'s results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Marcus Hale, Chief Development Officer; and Priya Singh, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Jordan, and good morning, everyone. AeroGreen Energy Corp. had a strong Q3, reflecting our commitment to innovation and sustainability in the renewable energy sector. We continue to see increasing demand for our clean energy solutions and are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing market opportunities.

We want to highlight five crucial aspects of this quarter's achievements. First, let's touch on our overall performance highlights and key achievements. I'm thrilled to start with these, as they underscore another standout quarter in a year of exceptional execution across our diversified clean energy portfolio. We delivered results that not only beat our guidance but also position us stronger than ever in the accelerating global energy transition. Consolidated revenue reached $1.42 billion, up 32% year-over-year and 8% above the high end of our Q3 guidance. This growth stemmed from a 45% surge in our Energy Generation & Services segment, fueled by higher merchant pricing in key ISO markets like CAISO and ERCOT, where average realized prices hit $58 per MWh—our strongest Q3 since 2022. Our Storage Solutions business grew 28%, reflecting robust demand for our next-gen lithium-iron-phosphate systems, optimized for 4-hour duration with 95% round-trip efficiency. EBITDA came in at $502 million, a 38% increase, expanding margins to 35.3% from 32.1% last year, thanks to optimized O&M costs and scale efficiencies in our 2.8 GWdc solar fleet. Adjusted EPS was $0.92, surpassing consensus by 15%, while our project backlog now stands at a record $28 billion, providing over four years of visibility at current run-rates.

Operationally, we hit several key milestones showcasing our technical leadership and execution prowess. We commissioned 1.2 GW of new capacity across our pipeline, including the 450 MWdc Desert Bloom Solar project in Arizona—the largest bifacial PV installation in the U.S. Southwest this year—leveraging TOPCon cell tech with 23.5% module efficiency, reducing our portfolio LCOE to $28 per MWh, competitive with new-build combined-cycle gas. In storage, we deployed 850 MWh of BESS across three fronts: a 300 MW/1,200 MWh facility in Texas integrated with our AI-driven Virtual Power Plant software, which optimized dispatch to capture $15 million in ancillary services revenue; a 200 MW/800 MWh hybrid wind-solar-storage project in the UK under the latest CfD auction; and our first 150 MW green hydrogen electrolyzer stack in partnership with Plug Power, achieving 65% stack efficiency on renewable inputs.

Regionally, performance was balanced and resilient. In the Americas, accounting for 62% of revenue, we capitalized on the IRA's Section 45X manufacturing credits, with our new 5 GW annual module fab in Ohio—mirroring First Solar's thin-film approach—now at 85% capacity utilization, generating $120 million in PTC-equivalent benefits. This helped us secure 15-year PPAs with hyperscalers like Google and Microsoft at IRRs north of 12%. EMEA contributed 24% of revenue, up 41% YoY, driven by REPowerEU tailwinds; our 300 MW onshore wind portfolio in Germany and Poland benefited from falling turbine costs, down 15% QoQ per IRENA data, and TSO curtailment reforms, yielding near-98% availability. APAC, at 14% of revenue, saw explosive growth in Australia and India, where we added 250 MW of floating solar on hydro reservoirs—a nod to Adani Green's model—amid grid congestion relief from AEMO's ISP roadmap.

Strategically, these achievements reflect our 'Scale, Stack, Store' framework. We've stacked $4.2 billion in new PPAs and contracts since Q1, including a landmark 10 GW framework with the Saudi PIF for green hydrogen exports, positioning us in the $1 trillion H2 economy per BloombergNEF forecasts. On innovation, our R&D spend hit $85 million this quarter, yielding breakthroughs like perovskite-silicon tandem cells at 30% efficiency in pilots, outpacing lab records, and VPP software that boosted fleet-wide EBITDA margins by 200 bps through ML-optimized curtailment avoidance. ESG-wise, we reduced Scope 1&2 emissions by 42% YoY via electrification of EPC fleets, earning an MSCI ESG 'AA' rating and unlocking $500 million in green bond financing at 4.2% yields. These highlights de-risk our FY2024 guidance: revenue of $5.4-5.6 billion, EBITDA $1.95-2.05 billion, with Q4 capacity adds of 1.5 GW. We're uniquely positioned amid favorable macros—global clean capex projected at $2 trillion through 2030 per IEA, with policy certainty from U.S. elections and EU's Net Zero Industry Act.

Second, on capacity factor performance by technology across solar PV, onshore and offshore wind, and battery energy storage systems. Capacity factor is a critical KPI for us, reflecting not just asset efficiency but our ability to deliver reliable, bankable energy into wholesale markets, PPAs, and ancillary services. Overall, our portfolio-wide average capacity factor came in at 34.2% for the quarter, up 180 basis points year-over-year and beating our internal guidance by 50 bps. This outperformance was driven by favorable resource years, aggressive tech upgrade initiatives, and enhanced O&M strategies leveraging AI-driven SCADA optimization.

For solar PV, representing 42% of our 12.5 GW operating portfolio, the fleet-wide capacity factor hit 27.8%, the strongest quarterly print since Q1 2022. This was propelled by a pristine resource year in our key markets—global horizontal irradiance averaged 5.9 kWh/m²/day across our Southwest U.S. and Australian assets, 8% above long-term averages per NREL datasets. In the U.S. Southwest, like California ISO and ERCOT zones, we saw 32.1% CF, benefiting from our 1.3 DC/AC ratio on recent builds and single-axis trackers from Array Technologies, with low curtailment at 1.2%—half the CAISO system average—thanks to our 15-minute ahead forecasting model integrated with NOAA data. Europe, in Spain and Italy PPAs, achieved 22.4% CF, tempered by a cloudy summer but up 150 bps YoY via bifacial PERC-to-TOPCon retrofits on 400 MW of legacy fleet; these N-type cells from LONGi deliver 4-6% higher energy yield per IEC 61724 standards. Australia shone at 29.3% CF, where hybrid solar-plus-storage projects like our 300 MWp Gunhoolba facility hit 31.2% thanks to 2200 MWh/acre land optimization. We've completed TOPCon module swaps on 25% of our pre-2022 portfolio, boosting specific yield by 5.2%, and we're piloting heterojunction tech from Huasun on a 100 MW testbed in Arizona, targeting 30%+ CF in high-DNI sites. We expect Q4 solar CF at 28.5%, with full-year 2024 averaging 27.2%—well ahead of the SEIA benchmark of 25.8% for utility-scale U.S. PV.

Wind assets, comprising 38% of our portfolio at 9.8 GW, posted robust results amid volatile wind regimes. Onshore fleet CF reached 37.4%, while our 2.1 GW offshore portfolio in the North Sea and U.S. East Coast delivered 47.9%—our best offshore quarter ever. Onshore in the U.S. Midwest/Plains, MISO/PJM, we hit 39.2% CF on Vestas V150-4.2 MW turbines, up from 37.8% YoY due to rotor upgrades increasing swept area by 15%, with capacity-weighted average hub-height winds at 8.1 m/s per AWS Truepower reanalysis. Europe, UK and Germany, saw 35.1% CF, pressured by 10% below-normal winds but mitigated by 20% deployment of Siemens Gamesa 6.X platforms with integral direct-drive tech, reducing wakes by 8%. Offshore highlights include North Sea UK Round 4 leases at 49.8% CF on our Orsted-partnered 600 MW Borkum Riff Two, leveraging 15 MW GE Haliade-X prototypes with 220m rotors, and U.S. Atlantic BOEM-approved sites at 45.2% CF, with Vineyard Wind 1 ramping to 48% post-commissioning. Larger rotors and taller hubs are compressing the CF gap between onshore and offshore to under 10 points for new builds. We've curtailed just 0.8% fleet-wide via dynamic yaw control and our proprietary WindOS AI suite, optimizing wakes 12% better than baseline per DNV audits. With IRA PTC extensions and EU REPowerEU subsidies, we're prioritizing repowerings—targeting 1 GW onshore in 2025 at 42%+ CF. Q4 guidance: onshore 38%, offshore 48.5%; full-year onshore at 37.1% vs. AWEA's 35.4% peer average.

For our 4.2 GWh BESS fleet, 24% of EBITDA contribution, we report an equivalent capacity factor based on average discharge power relative to nameplate—landing at 68.4% in Q3, up 12% YoY. This reflects high dispatchability in frequency regulation, arbitrage, and renewables firming, with round-trip efficiency at 92.1% across LG Chem and Tesla Megapack deployments. In CAISO/ERCOT, 2.1 GWh standalone plus hybrid, utilization was 72%, capturing $150/MWh arbitrage spreads during heatwaves; our 850 MW/3.4 GWh Moss Landing expansion, the world's largest, achieved 91.5% RTE with thermal management upgrades. Australia saw 65% utilization in FCAS markets, bolstered by 10% degradation mitigation via electrolyte recirculation pilots. UK/Europe hit 62% utilization, focused on T-4 capacity auctions amid National Grid ESO reforms. Initiatives include LFP cell adoption, 95% of new builds for 4,000+ cycles at 80% DoD, and VPP aggregation with Stem's Athena AI for 15% uplift in revenue stacking. Degradation averaged 1.8% YoD, below CATL warranty curves. Hybrids are key—our 80% solar/wind co-located BESS saw 75% CF equivalent vs. 55% standalone peers per EIA data. We're guiding Q4 at 70% utilization, full-year at 67.5%, with 2 GW/8 GWh additions in 2025 targeting 92.5% RTE.

Across technologies, hybrid co-location drove 22% of our CF uplift—solar plus storage firming wind intermittency. Our GreenAI platform cut imbalance penalties 18%, while PPAs with corporates like Google and Amazon embed performance bonuses tied to 95% P90 availability. Risks like supply chain snarls on HVDC transformers or La Niña impacts are hedged with our $50M weather derivative book, but with $2.3B capex guidance intact, we're on track for portfolio CF expansion to 36% by 2026, fueled by 5 GW new builds and 40% tech refresh cadence.

Third, new PPAs secured and average PPA price—a key bright spot in our commercial execution. PPAs remain the bedrock of our renewable energy backlog, providing long-duration revenue visibility in a volatile merchant market. In Q3 alone, we secured 1.8 GW of new PPAs, bringing year-to-date total to 4.2 GW—that's a 35% increase over last year and on track to exceed our full-year guidance of 5 GW. The standout was a 750 MW hybrid solar-plus-storage PPA with Microsoft for Desert Bloom in CAISO, a 20-year agreement at all-in $42 per MWh, escalating 2% annually with CPI, including dispatchable firm power from 300 MW/1,200 MWh of our four-hour LFP battery systems, leveraging bifacial PERC modules with 1.4:1 DC:AC ratio for enhanced yield, targeting over 32% first-year capacity factor with our AI-optimized curtailment forecasting post-AB 2514 reforms.

We also locked in 650 MW of standalone utility-scale solar PPAs in ERCOT with a leading hyperscaler, akin to Amazon's RE100 commitments, at an average $31/MWh over 15 years. Internationally, a 400 MW onshore wind PPA in the UK's Net Zero Teeside zone, counterpartied by Orsted-inspired green hydrogen offtake, at £52/MWh or roughly $65/MWh equivalent—a premium reflecting energy security post-Ukraine and TCFD-mandated Scope 2 decarbonization. For these new Q3 contracts, we achieved a blended $38 per MWh average, down 12% YoY from $43/MWh, continuing a multi-year downtrend from TOPCon module prices plummeting 45% YTD to under $0.22/Wp due to Southeast Asia overcapacity, offset by IRA 45X PTC/ITC adders unlocking 10-15% yield uplifts for U.S.-manufactured trackers from Nextracker partners. Our all-in LCOE for new solar now $28-32/MWh, yielding 12-14% unlevered IRRs above our 8% hurdle.

U.S. pricing held resilient: CAISO at $45/MWh with LCFS credit stacking and NEM 3.0 VPP synergies; ERCOT at $30/MWh hedging negative pricing; PJM/MISO at $36/MWh amid queue reforms fast-tracking our 2.5 GW interconnections. Europe firmed 8% QoQ to €48/MWh on REPowerEU and Russian gas displacement. Our 'PPA-Plus' playbook features 85% investment-grade corporate offtakers like Microsoft, Google, Apple; 70% take-or-pay with 5-year extensions and merchant upside sharing above $25/MWh collar, protecting $45 million EBITDA last year. Contracted backlog at 12.3 GW through 2045, 60% back-loaded into 2027+. Our 15 GW PPA pipeline, 40% advanced, targets $35-40/MWh in 2025 with stabilizing ASPs and 20% storage cost drops, prioritizing hybrids and green H2 tie-ins like our 500 MW Mojave Hydrogen Hub bid. These wins validate our tech-enabled cost curve leadership for 20% CAGR backlog growth.

Fourth, debt levels and financing costs—a critical pillar of our capital structure in this capital-intensive Clean Tech sector. Our disciplined approach to financing supports aggressive growth in offshore wind, utility-scale solar PV, emerging BESS, and green hydrogen platforms, navigating a higher-for-longer interest rate environment. As of September 30th, total gross debt stood at $5.2 billion, comprising $1.1 billion in short-term facilities and revolver draws—primarily for construction working capital on our 1.2 GW U.S. East Coast offshore wind pipeline—and $4.1 billion in long-term project finance and corporate debt. This structure keeps our net debt-to-EBITDA at a healthy 3.2x, down from 3.8x at year-start, reflecting strong FCF generation of $350 million in Q3 from stabilized merchant exposures and IRA tax equity flips.

Financing costs averaged 4.8% blended in Q3, up 60 bps YoY but below peers thanks to 65% fixed-rate project debt tied to SOFR + 150 bps on green bonds issued under our EMTN program. We've locked 80% of draws through 2025 at sub-5% via interest rate swaps, hedging $1.5 billion exposure. Recent wins include a $800 million construction facility for Desert Bloom at SOFR + 175 bps, fully non-recourse with DOE loan guarantees covering 30% of capex under Title 17 Innovative Clean Energy. Corporate revolver utilization at 25%, with $1.2 billion undrawn capacity providing ample liquidity for 2 GW Q4 energizations.

Our strategy emphasizes project-level non-recourse financing—90% of portfolio debt—leveraging asset quality with 98% debt service coverage ratios. We've tapped $600 million in sustainability-linked bonds at 4.2% yields, tied to SBTi-validated emission cuts, and are advancing a $1 billion securitization of stabilized solar cash flows akin to NRG's model. Forward, with capex peaking at $2.3 billion in 2025, we target leverage below 3x via $1.5 billion tax equity raises and 20% FCF retention. Risks like rate volatility are mitigated by our $200 million cap on floating exposure and early refinancing of $500 million 2022 Term Loan B at 6.2%.

Fifth, our strategic priorities and outlook for the next quarter and year, underscoring our leadership in integrated clean energy solutions from utility-scale solar and wind to advanced BESS and green hydrogen. We've outperformed the sector with 28% YoY revenue growth to $1.42 billion in Q3, driven by our 5.2 GW project backlog and robust margins from our diversified portfolio; adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 32% ahead of peers like NextEra and Orsted, thanks to optimized O&M and favorable hedging on our 1.8 GW wind fleet amid stabilizing turbine supply chains.

For Q4 2024, focus is on execution and derisking amid elevated rates and softening commodities. Priorities include accelerating 1.2 GW solar-plus-storage deployments, like the 450 MW Desert Bloom hybrid in California with bifacial TOPCon modules at 22.5% efficiency from JinkoSolar and 200 MWh LFP BESS from CATL, leveraging IRA 45Z/48E ITCs for LCOE below $25/MWh. BESS scale-up targets $250 million Q4 revenue from 800 MWh queue in frequency regulation and arbitrage, boosted by AI-driven EMS improving dispatch 18%. Supply chain resilience ramps our $500 million Nevada gigafactory for perovskite-silicon tandems targeting 30%+ efficiency by mid-2025; Q4 capex $180 million, funded by cash flows and $2 billion undrawn revolver.

North America drives 65% backlog via IRA corporate PPAs—15 new 2.1 GW deals with tech giants mirroring Google's 24/7 carbon-free goals. Europe sees REPowerEU support for 600 MW North Sea offshore, $80 million Q4 contribution despite permitting. APAC grows via electrolyzer exports to Australia's Hydrogen Headstart. Q4 guidance: revenue $1.35-1.45 billion, up 15-20% QoQ; EBITDA $420-460 million at 31-33% margin; FCF $300 million post-capex, with $50 million weather tailwind from Pacific Northwest hydro.

For FY2025, we guide 25-30% revenue growth to $5.8-6.2 billion, EBITDA margins 34-36% via operating leverage and upgrades. 10 GW pipeline, up 20%, supports 3 GW annual adds outpacing WoodMac forecasts. Pillars: $1.2 billion R&D/capex for green H2 via PEM electrolyzers targeting $1.50/kg and long-duration iron-air BESS with Form Energy for 20% ancillary upside. Market expansion into India 500 MW solar EPC under PM Surya Ghar, 15% APAC mix by 2026; U.S. ERCOT bids for 1 GW hybrids at $45-50/MWh amid data center growth. Sustainability targets SBTi 50% Scope 1/2 cuts via fleet electrification and 95% turbine blade circularity, enhancing MSCI 'AA' for $1.5 billion green bonds sub-4%. M&A with $800 million for trading software and C&I solar to double 500 MW DG backlog.

Supporting trends: BNEF solar LCOE to $20/MWh, wind CF to 45%+, BESS to 100 GWh. Risks like tariffs mitigated by 70% domestic content, bipartisan IRA exposure. We're raising FY2024 EPS to $4.85-5.05, initiating FY2025 at $6.20-6.60—AeroGreen blending scale with disruptive tech for shareholder value in $1.7 trillion TAM.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to provide a detailed overview of our financial performance.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Elena. We are pleased with our financial results for Q3. Revenue reached $1.42 billion, representing a 32% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by the successful commissioning of several new projects and higher energy production. Our gross margin improved to 35.3%, reflecting our efforts to optimize operational efficiency and manage costs effectively. Operating expenses totaled $420 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and expansion into new markets. Net income was $285 million, or $0.92 per share. We maintained a strong balance sheet with $1.8 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our financial outlook for the remainder of the year remains positive.

Now, I'll pass the call to Marcus Hale to discuss our project development pipeline.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Sarah. Our project development pipeline continues to grow, with 15 GW of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies, including solar PV, onshore and offshore wind, BESS hybrids, and early-stage green hydrogen. We're making significant progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements—over 40% of the pipeline is at advanced notice-to-proceed stages. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters, including 1.5 GW in Q4, which will further contribute to our revenue growth and profitability. We're also exploring opportunities to expand our project portfolio through strategic acquisitions and partnerships, such as our recent JV with a major hyperscaler for 2 GW of data center-backed renewables and potential bolt-ons in high-growth regions like India and the U.S. Gulf Coast.

Next, Priya Singh will provide an update on our sustainability initiatives.

Priya Singh:
Thank you, Marcus. Sustainability is at the core of our business, and we are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and contributing to a cleaner, more sustainable future. In Q3, we made significant progress, achieving a 42% year-over-year reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions through full electrification of our EPC fleets and procurement of 100% renewable-powered construction sites. Energy efficiency improvements across our operating assets, driven by AI-optimized O&M, saved 15% on portfolio-wide consumption. We're promoting responsible resource management, with 95% circularity in turbine blade recycling and water usage down 28% via dry-cooling retrofits on solar plants. Community engagement remains strong—we supported 50+ local initiatives, investing $12 million in workforce training for clean tech jobs and biodiversity offsets at offshore sites. These efforts earned us an MSCI ESG 'AA' rating and positioned us for premium green financing. We believe our sustainability initiatives not only benefit the environment but also create long-term value for our stakeholders.

I'll now turn the call back to Elena for closing remarks.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Priya. In conclusion, we are very pleased with our performance this quarter. We are confident that our strategic initiatives and our commitment to innovation and sustainability will drive continued growth and success in the years to come.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Can you discuss the impact of supply chain constraints on your project timelines?

Marcus Hale:
Thanks, John. Supply chain constraints remain a headwind, particularly for HVDC transformers and select BESS components, where lead times have stretched to 18 months amid global demand surges. However, we've derisked this through forward contracts covering 85% of 2025 module needs with U.S. and allied suppliers, and our Nevada gigafactory insulates against polysilicon volatility. This has delayed two offshore integrations by one quarter, but our critical path projects like Desert Bloom remain on schedule for Q4 energization. We're also qualifying secondary sources in India and Vietnam, targeting a 20% cost buffer in bids. Overall, timelines are holding within 5% of plan, supported by $100 million in inventory pre-builds.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
What is your strategy for expanding into emerging markets?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Great question, Emily. Emerging markets like India and Saudi Arabia represent 15-20% of our long-term growth, leveraging our 'Scale, Stack, Store' model. In India, we're bidding 500 MW solar EPC under PM Surya Ghar, partnering local TATA Power for grid ties, targeting $35/MWh PPAs with rooftop hybrids. Saudi PIF's 10 GW H2 framework positions us for $1.50/kg exports via PEM electrolyzers on solar curtailment. Strategy emphasizes JVs for permitting speed—70% local content—and stacking incentives like India's PLI scheme. We expect 1 GW deployed by 2026, adding $400 million annual EBITDA at 35% margins, with risks like FX hedged via dollar-denominated offtakes.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
How are you managing the increasing competition in the renewable energy sector?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
David, competition is intensifying, but our tech edge and execution set us apart. We differentiate via hybrids—80% of new builds co-locate storage, capturing 20% baseload premiums peers miss—and AI platforms like GreenAI/WindOS boosting CF 200 bps above industry averages. Cost leadership from domestic manufacturing yields 12-14% IRRs at $38/MWh PPAs, while our 15 GW pipeline and $28 billion backlog provide scale few match. M&A dry powder targets C&I and software tuck-ins, and ESG leadership unlocks green capital at 4% yields. We're outpacing peers on returns, guiding 25% CAGR through superior siting and corporate offtake focus.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Dr. Elena Vasquez for any closing remarks.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of AeroGreen Energy Corp. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
